messages.text: GekkoAxe GT would not start. Giving Hardware fault.
Searched the web · GekkoAxe GT "hardware fault" AxeOS

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. I'll check the GekkoAxe GT with you first.

"Hardware fault" on its own doesn't tell us much. The GekkoAxe GT runs AxeOS, and AxeOS shows that message for several different problems, from a weak power supply to the chips not answering. On a GT the cause is very often the power supply, not the miner. The detail shown with the message tells us which one it is.

**One thing to start with:**

1. Plug the GT in and let it start.
2. When "Hardware fault" appears, take a clear photo of the small screen, including any line or code below the message.
3. If you can still open the miner's web page from your browser, a screenshot of the error or the Logs page works too.

Send the photo or screenshot here and I'll take the next step from there.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Searched the web · "set_fan" "EMC2101 ID" board_prepare "fan setup" "ASIC rails
Searched the web · GekkoAxe GT EMC2101 fan controller error firmware

Hal here. I've gone through your log, and it's encouraging.

**What the log shows:**
- Network and pool are fine. It connects to us-east.harlolabs.com:8888, authorization is accepted and it receives jobs.
- Each time right after that, it fails on the fan controller: "set_fan: EMC2101 ID", then "fan setup" and "fan channel 1 could not be stopped".
- Because the fan can't be controlled, the firmware shuts off power to the chips ("ASIC rails disabled") as a safety step and ends the session. That loop is the "Hardware fault" you're seeing.

**Why this is probably not a broken board:** The firmware is looking for an EMC2101 fan controller. But according to the GekkoAxe firmware docs, the 
GekkoAxe-GT
 has an 
EMC2103
 fan controller. The EMC2101 is the part on the single-chip GekkoAxe Gamma. Combined with the "gpio: conflict found for GPIO[1]" line, this usually means the firmware thinks it's running on a different board than a GT. The chips are never even powered, so nothing points to them being damaged.

**Next check:**
1. Open the miner's web page and go to the **Settings** or **System** page.
2. Send me a screenshot showing the **firmware name and version** and the **board version / device model** it lists.

If that confirms the board setting is wrong, the fix should be reinstalling the correct stock firmware for the GT, not a return. I'll walk you through that once I see the screenshot.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Searched the web · GekkoScience GekkoAxe GT official firmware ESP-Miner github

Thanks, the photo is clear. The screen shows **"HARDWARE PROBLEM / BOARD INITIALIZATION FAILED / OPEN DASHBOARD"** on a board printed **GekkoAxe V2.1 GT, 12VDC**.

That matches the log. The miner stops at the "board prepare" step, when it tries to set up the fan controller. It never gets as far as powering the chips. So far this still looks like the firmware not matching the board, rather than the board being damaged.

There's a likely reason for that. GekkoScience, who designed the GekkoAxe, describes it as running AxeOS, but 
at least up to 2.10 out of the box, but the electronics are actually quite different
 from a Bitaxe. A firmware version or build made for standard Bitaxe hardware can look for parts the GT doesn't have, and the EMC2101 fan controller in your log is one of them.

**Next step:** The screen says "Open dashboard," so:

1. In your browser, open the miner's IP address (the same page your log came from).
2. Go to **Settings** (or **System**) and send me a screenshot of the section showing the **firmware version**, **board version** and **device model**.
3. Tell me whether the firmware was updated or changed at any point before this started, and to what.

With that I can tell you exactly which firmware your GT needs to get back to.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

That's the dashboard's version of the same message: **"HARDWARE PROBLEM, BOARD INITIALIZATION FAILED."** The note under it says dismissing it won't restart mining or turn off the safety protections. So clicking **Dismiss** is safe. It just closes the pop-up so you can get to the rest of the dashboard.

**Next step:**

1. Click **Dismiss**.
2. Open **Settings** (or **System** / **Info**, depending on the menu).
3. Send me a screenshot showing the **firmware name and version**, the **board version** and the **device model**.

Also, do you remember whether the firmware was updated or changed before this started? That plus the version should tell us which firmware your GT needs to get back to.
